insights.insight: Crinkl has crossed $1.43M in cryptographically verified gross merchandise value across ~24,800 receipts — a concrete scale proof that the protocol is processing real consumer spend, not modeled proxies.

The industry pays $5+ CPM to infer purchase intent from behavioral signals; a DKIM-verified receipt is cryptographic confirmation a transaction closed — the delta between inference and proof is where this protocol's data premium lives.

Average basket size has compressed from ~$80 to ~$58–60 over several months, driven by mix shift toward grocery and convenience — brands in those categories are generating proportionally more signal volume, while premium-ticket advertisers should note GMV growth now requires higher receipt throughput.

Week-over-week acceleration has held above 1.0x for multiple consecutive readings, meaning the growth rate itself is increasing even as token velocity oscillates in a stable 0.709–0.798x band — early-stage compounding, not plateau.

The protocol produces aggregate-queryable spend tokens without attaching consumer identity — a structural distinction from credit card networks, receipt loyalty apps, and data brokers, all of which require identity linkage to function.

Coverage spans 17–29 CBSAs per measurement window with pulse-based rather than linear expansion, suggesting density builds in clusters before spreading — relevant for brands planning regional activation against verified spend data.
